clue.text: Big shot in the film industry?

definitions.text: Big shot in the film industry?

parts.words: Big shot in the film industry
parts.note: a 'big shot' sounds like an important person in films, but here it is a camera shot in which the subject fills the frame

explanation.walkthrough: 'Big shot' suggests a movie mogul; the question mark hints the shot is a literal camera shot taken from very near.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph or film frame taken at very short range makes its subject look large, the literal big shot.

clue.text: Sweet student, American, beginning to consolidate debts

parts.note: L is the learner plate, standing for a student

indicators.note: the beginning of a word means only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of consolidate
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: A student, an American one, sweetly starting to sort out what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Luscious describes food that is richly sweet and delicious, a near synonym of sweet.

clue.text: Son with scam: teen regularly affected

parts.note: a scam is a trick or con

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word teen is taken

parts.note: second and fourth letters of teen

explanation.surface: A son who has been conned, an adolescent badly hit by the fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stricken by illness or grief is badly affected by it; the words are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Insured in secret

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as '...', protected by an insurance policy
second meaning: acting covertly, as a spy does

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words: an insured house is under cover of its policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under cover means protected by insurance, while undercover work is carried out covertly.

clue.text: Doctor gets round ban

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A medic gets round a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is an official refusal or prohibition, so a ban.

clue.text: Entertaining girl during voyage is hard

indicators.note: during says the answer sits inside the words voyage is hard

parts.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: A girl who keeps people amused while a hard sea journey goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained to entertain guests with music, dance and conversation.

clue.text: Well-informed, as a crossword is finished

definitions.meaning: first meaning: knowledgeable, in the know
second meaning: a finished crossword has all its entries clued, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase literally: once every light has a clue, the puzzle's setting is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To be clued up is an informal idiom for being knowledgeable about something.

clue.text: Animal, European, in more colourful surroundings

indicators.note: in places the European letter within the word for more colourful

parts.note: redder, more vivid in colour

explanation.surface: A European animal, with brighter colours all around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The red deer is a large species of deer found across Europe, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Signal to stir Reverend East, unwell before start of Eucharist

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
ill means unwell

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter only

parts.note: first letter of Eucharist

explanation.surface: A vicar feeling poorly before the communion service gets a wake-up call.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning, a signal to get up.

clue.text: A way to travel on a horse?

parts.note: a stride is a long step, one way of getting about on foot

explanation.surface: A question about whether riding is a good way of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether riding is a way to travel; in fact 'A way to travel' is the wordplay and 'on a horse?' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits astride a horse, one leg on each side, so astride means mounted on it.

clue.text: Suspend revolutionary press in part of China

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for suspend is read backwards

parts.note: to stop is to suspend or halt
a press is a crowd, a herd of people

explanation.surface: An order to shut down rebel newspapers in a Chinese province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' at the start of the sentence hides its lower-case sense: china crockery, of which a potsherd is a broken piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a fragment of broken pottery, so a piece of china.

clue.text: Flier's here naked, peering around outside

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go round the middle of here
around means the letters of peering are moved about
naked means stripped of its outer letters, so only the middle of here is kept

parts.note: middle letters of here

explanation.surface: A bird stares about from here, bare of feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' leaves ER from here; 'around' rearranges peering to PEGRINE; 'outside' wraps that round ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine is a falcon, a bird and so a flier; it is famed as the fastest diving bird.

clue.text: Harry perhaps moving right to the end to find nipper

indicators.note: moving says a letter leaves its place in the word for Harry perhaps
to the end says where that right letter is put back, at the close of the word

parts.note: Prince Harry is an example of a prince

explanation.surface: A royal shifting position to find a young child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' suggests a small child, a sense that suits a royal; here it is a claw that pinches.
explanation.definitionFit: A pincer is the claw of a crab or lobster, something that nips.

clue.text: Unrealistic drawing of vehicle — one Jaguar, maybe, by river

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral for one
a jaguar is an example of a big cat
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A cartoon of a car, a Jaguar perhaps, parked by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaguar is also a car make, which the surface plays on; here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricature exaggerates features for comic effect, so it is a deliberately unrealistic picture.

clue.text: Animals are barred from crossing this

definitions.text: Animals are barred from crossing this

parts.words: Animals are barred from crossing this
parts.note: barred suggests forbidden, but the device is literally made of bars that livestock cannot walk over

explanation.walkthrough: 'barred' reads as banned, yet it is literal: the grid's bars over a pit stop hooves.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle grid is a set of metal bars over a road ditch that livestock will not cross but vehicles can.

clue.text: Pipe potato, briefly?

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, its last letter lost

parts.note: a potato is a tuber

explanation.surface: A short query about piping mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube is a hollow cylinder that carries liquid or gas, the same as a pipe.

clue.text: Pilot or labourer with spat reported

indicators.note: reported says the words are spoken aloud to give a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a navvy is a labourer and a spat is a short gaiter worn over the shoe; said together they run into one word

explanation.surface: A pilot or a workman involved in a reported quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spat' looks like a quarrel but is the old ankle covering, a gaiter. Navvy is British for a road or canal labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator steers or plots a course, the role of a pilot guiding a ship.

clue.text: Composition in which harp plays so extremely daintily

indicators.note: plays means the letters of harp are rearranged, as if played about with
extremely means only the outermost letters of daintily are used

parts.note: first and last letters of daintily

explanation.surface: A piece of music in which the harpist performs with great delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is a free-flowing musical work, one type of composition.

clue.text: Turn goes badly for swimmer

indicators.note: badly means the letters of turn goes are jumbled

explanation.surface: A swimmer whose tumble turn goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturgeon is a large fish, and a fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: Staff showing respect that's out of the ordinary

indicators.note: out of the ordinary means unusual, so the letters of respect are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Employees showing an unusual degree of deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests workers; here it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is the ornamental rod a monarch carries, a ceremonial staff.

clue.text: Hold the setter up, and get ready!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so me
to brace yourself is to get ready for something

explanation.surface: A command to grab the puzzle's setter and prepare for impact.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is to hold them in your arms; a hug or clasp.

clue.text: Dislike part of match at Edgbaston

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Disliking a section of a cricket game at Edgbaston, the Birmingham Test ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate is strong aversion, so a stronger synonym of dislike.

clue.text: Traveller's TV advert?

parts.note: the salesman on the road was once known by a word that also names a paid slot between TV programmes

explanation.walkthrough: A travelling salesman was once called a commercial traveller; the word also names a TV advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial is a television advertisement, and the same word qualifies a salesman on the road.

clue.text: Team consumed by anger over magic potion

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the whole is turned upside down, reversed
consumed by means the team is swallowed inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A furious side gulping down a magic drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down clue turns the whole assembly upside down, so the team sits in the anger word before it is read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a magical liquid said to prolong life or cure all ills.

clue.text: Member in country realm

indicators.note: in places the member inside the country's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A member of parliament in a country's kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a territory ruled by an emperor, a domain or kingdom, so a realm.

clue.text: Time to serve breakfast food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a prison sentence
second meaning: oat cereal cooked in milk or water

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like breakfast is ready; 'doing porridge' is British slang for serving prison time.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang for a jail term and the hot oat cereal eaten in the morning share one word.

clue.text: Info about large valley in Scotland

indicators.note: about means the information word goes round the letter for large

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Details on a big Scottish valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, the term used especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Statement backed imprisoning old soldier

indicators.note: imprisoning means the reversed word holds the letter for old
backed means turned back to front, read in reverse

parts.note: a report is a statement

explanation.surface: A statement in support of jailing an old soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' sounds like supported, but means reversed: REPORT becomes TROPER, and 'imprisoning' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private in a cavalry or armoured regiment, so a soldier.

clue.text: One getting the present set

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a recipient of a gift
second meaning: a radio or television set

explanation.walkthrough: The 'present' is a gift; the 'set' is a radio or TV apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiver is a person who receives something, and also the apparatus that picks up broadcast signals.

clue.text: Edward, languishing, going round and round

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the name Edward
languishing, wasting away, can mean dying

explanation.surface: Edward, wasting away, spinning in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Water eddying swirls in circular currents, moving in a whirl.
